## Iteration 1 acceptance

See [the explicit bounded acceptance record](research/roadmap/iteration-01/ACCEPTANCE.md).

Four tags preserve string, boolean, signed int64 and finite binary64 identity throughout literals, interning, every derived position, hashing/joins, ordering, storage and results. There is no cross-tag coercion. Floats normalize negative zero; full int64 and temporal JSON coordinates use canonical decimal strings. NUL/invalid UTF-8/nonfinite values and unsupported families fail explicitly. Migrated values always remain strings, preserving physical history, IDs, receipts, clock and timestamps.

Real checks pass: 57 typed native integration cases, 29 independent SQL/native cases (including permutations/duplicates and ambient collation controls), 22 legacy native cases, 23 legacy storage cases, 26 genuine migration acceptance cases, 96 browser groups and 122 unchanged external browser-contract checks. Categories overlap; this is not a combined certification score. The legacy metadata assertion alone intentionally changes extension version 0.1.0 to 0.2.0.

The core normal and ASan/UBSan campaigns include 12,024 exact frozen/current rows, counters and errors, 515 focused typed checks, 20 golden answers, eight parser rejections, mixed-tag graph oracles and bounded fuzzing. The actual instrumented v2 binding also passes all 57 native cases. Leak detection is explicitly off; prebuilt DuckDB/Python are not fully instrumented. Historical helper/runtime setup failures remain separate from final passes.

Browser iterator/getter/Proxy admission defects were corrected and independently retested. Genuine missing-artifact coverage uses a fresh copied project with its own real ROOT, no monkeypatch/path-policy relaxation: persistence/reopen work, queries report NativeUnavailable, and evaluation failure rolls back the command.

## Research, measured performance and negative results

Initial [typed-domain study](research/roadmap/iteration-01/typed-values-research.md) and [representation study](research/roadmap/iteration-01/performance.md) preceded implementation. The user pivot reopened the [actual-v2 semantics](research/roadmap/iteration-01/unstable-api-pivot/semantics.md) and [mechanisms/performance](research/roadmap/iteration-01/unstable-api-pivot/performance.md) gate. Later transport/source and sanitizer-runtime blockers received further primary-source research.

The first balanced study retains 1,188 fully checked measured samples in 54 isolated processes and its observed 23–36% losses in two cases. A tighter 756-pair/1,512-sample CPU-pinned serial A/B study across both load orders and two processes does not reproduce a large causal API regression (roughly 0.97–1.03x paired medians). Both data sets remain preserved; process/host drift is material. No universal speedup is claimed.

Typed STRUCT-to-Python result conversion is separately costly. A same-statement compact UNION projection preserved exact semantics/snapshots but was 1.71–1.87x slower in recursive full-fetch controls and was not adopted. Source-supported sizing/mask/validation optimizations remain proposals, not demonstrated causal fixes or shipped speculative changes.

The direct-v2 quota failure led to fresh official documentation and an independent Python real-file reproduction: connect-time max_temp_directory_size can be reported but ignored. Applying the identical intended bound after connect enforces it. The corrective live SET is tested; it is not full private-memory/process accounting. Ambiguous BETWEEN pushdown remains declined until exact semantics are established; table hooks are not a general optimizer rewrite API.
